title: Restore a corporation property licence
summary: This page explains how to apply to restore a corporation property licence if it has expired within the last three months.
intro:
If your corporation property licence has expired within the last 3 months, you can apply to have it restored.

If you do not apply for a restoration within 3 months, you’ll need to apply for a new licence. You cannot trade until the new licence is issued.
who_can_apply: The corporation property licence must have expired within the last 3 months.
what_you_need: Renewal number (as shown on the renewal notice)
Two forms of identification (Note: If you do not have two forms of identification listed above, you may still be eligible. Contact NSW Fair Trading for more information.)

how_to_steps.text: Follow the prompts to restore the corporation property licence.

external_links.text: Information for property professionals – NSW Fair Trading

faqs.q: What happens if my licence expires?
faqs.a: If your licence has expired within the last 3 months, you can apply to have it restored. If you do not apply for a restoration within 3 months, you will need to apply for a new licence, and you cannot trade until the new licence is issued.

faqs.q: How do I restore my licence?
faqs.a: Select the ‘Restore online’ button and follow the prompts to restore the corporation property licence.

faqs.q: What do I need to restore my licence?
faqs.a: You need your corporation property licence number, renewal number, your personal and corporation details, fee payment, and two forms of identification.
